name: Spin a basketball on your finger
blurb: A quick win. The technique is entirely about spin speed and finding the ball’s true axis, then learning to feed it more spin with your free hand.
gear: A basketball, slightly under-inflated is easier
steps: Find the axis: hold the ball with the valve as a reference and spin it in the air to see which orientation is stable.
Practise a strong flick spin with both hands, catching it on your palm first to feel the axis.
Move to the fingernail, not the fingertip pad — the nail gives a much lower-friction point.
Learn the feed: brush the ball with the fingers of your free hand in the direction of spin to top up the speed.
Practise transferring the ball from the palm to the fingernail without losing the axis.
tips: Not enough initial spin is the usual cause of failure, not finger position.
A fully pumped-up ball is harder. Let a little air out while learning.
proof: You spin the ball for ten seconds on one finger, feeding it at least twice.
